h1: The 6 Best Dehumidifiers Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six compact dehumidifiers under $100, compared on tank size, quiet operation, safety shutoff and coverage.
summary: The 58 oz Small Dehumidifier with a 230 sq ft rating is our top pick for the largest listed tank and defrost protection. The NeedDuck 44 oz is the quiet-minded runner-up, while the NineSky, OWAAE and BEDRED add auto shutoff for bedrooms and bathrooms. All six cost under $100.
intro: Small dehumidifiers under $100 are not like the big compressor units, and the mistake is expecting them to be. They suit a bedroom, closet or bathroom, and the tank size and shutoff behavior decide whether you will actually like living with one.

We reviewed six compact units and ranked them on listed tank size, coverage, safety features and noise claims. Every one sits under the $100 mark. We left out a near-duplicate listing of one TABYIK model.

products.name: Dehumidifier 1657ML 58OZ Small Dehumidifier for Home 230 Ft² Safety
products.verdict: The largest listed tank, with defrost and safety protection.
products.description:
This dehumidifier has a 1657 ml (58 oz) tank, a 230 sq ft coverage rating, and defrosting plus safety protection. It offers three setting modes with quiet operation, and costs $25 to $50.

The tank is the largest among the six, which means fewer trips to the sink. It is also the only one here that lists a square-foot coverage figure.

It suits a bedroom or small room. The caveat is that 230 sq ft is a small-room rating.

products.name: NeedDuck Dehumidifier for Home Small Quiet Dehumidifiers for 44OZ Water Tank
products.verdict: A quiet, compact unit with a 44 oz tank and built-in safety.
products.description:
The NeedDuck is a compact, portable dehumidifier with a 44 oz water tank, built-in safety and convenience features, and a quiet design. It costs $25 to $50.

It gives up 14 oz of tank capacity to the pick above, and in exchange the listing emphasizes quiet use over rapid moisture removal. That is a deliberate tradeoff.

It suits light moisture in bedrooms. The caveat is that it is not built for fast removal.

products.name: OWAAE Dehumidifier for Home with Auto Shutoff Sleep Mode
products.verdict: Auto shutoff and a sleep mode for nighttime use.
products.description:
The OWAAE offers auto shutoff, a sleep mode and an ultra-quiet design aimed at bedrooms and nighttime comfort. The listing also says it suits bathrooms and enclosed spaces. It costs $50 to $100.

It costs more than the first two picks yet lists no tank size, so you pay for the sleep mode and shutoff. That is the tradeoff.

It suits light sleepers. The caveat is the missing capacity figure.

products.name: NineSky Dehumidifiers for Home
products.verdict: A quiet unit with smart auto shut-off protection.
products.description:
The NineSky is a quiet, high-efficiency dehumidifier with smart auto shut-off protection, in the $50 to $100 range.

Compared with the OWAAE it offers a similar quiet and shutoff story but with less emphasis on sleep. The listing gives no tank or coverage figure.

It suits general home use. The caveat is the thin spec detail.

products.name: BEDRED Dehumidifier
products.verdict: A semiconductor model with auto shutoff and a 7-color light.
products.description:
The BEDRED is a semiconductor dehumidifier that uses thermoelectric cooling, with intelligent auto shutoff and a 7-color ambient light. It costs $50 to $100.

Its thermoelectric design is the distinguishing detail against the rest, and the ambient light is a styling extra. The listing gives no tank size.

It suits small spaces where style matters. The caveat is the missing capacity detail.

products.name: ToLife Dehumidifier
products.verdict: A powerful mode and seven ambient light colors.
products.description:
The ToLife offers a powerful mode and seven ambient light colors, in the $50 to $100 range.

It is last because the listing leans on lighting rather than stated tank, coverage or shutoff details. The powerful mode is the one performance feature mentioned.

It suits buyers who like ambient lights. The caveat is the sparse spec sheet.

whatMatters.detail: The tank is the water it holds before it needs emptying. A bigger tank means fewer trips. Look for ounces or milliliters in the title.
Coverage in square feet shows the room size it targets. Only one model here lists it, at 230 sq ft. Match it to your room.
A full-tank cutoff keeps water from spilling while nobody is home. Check the listing for the words auto shutoff.
Quiet matters in bedrooms. Listings here make quiet claims without decibel figures, so treat them as claims. Check reviews for real feedback.
Thermoelectric units use a semiconductor, as on the BEDRED. They suit small spaces. Check the type in the description.

faq.q: How large a room will these cover?
faq.a: Only the 58 oz model lists coverage, at 230 sq ft. The others do not, so treat them as small-room units.
Expecting a compact unit to dry a whole basement. These suit small spaces.

faq.q: Is a bigger tank worth it?
faq.a: Yes if you hate emptying. The 58 oz model lists the largest tank among the six.
Follow the instructions. The listings we reviewed do not describe the steps.

faq.q: Do I need to clean it?
faq.a: Follow the maker's care guide. The listings do not give a cleaning routine.
The OWAAE lists a sleep mode and auto shutoff for nighttime use. Check others on the product page.

finalTake: The 58 oz Small Dehumidifier is the best value under $100 for a small room. The NeedDuck suits quiet bedrooms, and the OWAAE adds sleep mode. Expect small-room performance from all of them.
